title: Acute Stress Episode
interpretation: A single-day spike in stress score above 70 with corresponding recovery score drop below 40 indicates an acute stress response. This is normal during demanding work, conflicts, or stressful events. The body's stress response is adaptive in the short term. Concern arises only if it does not resolve within 24-48 hours.
recommended_agent_action: Log as single occurrence. If stress resolves within 48 hours and recovery rebounds, no action needed. If sustained, begin tracking as pattern.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude anxiety disorder or chronic stress from a single stressful day.

title: Accumulated Stress Load
interpretation: When stress scores remain elevated above personal baseline by 50%+ for 7 or more consecutive days while recovery scores remain suppressed and HRV declines, the user is experiencing accumulated stress load. This state increases vulnerability to illness, emotional dysregulation, and physical injury.
recommended_agent_action: Escalate to Level 3 concern. Provide the user with a summary of the trend. Ask about contributing factors. Suggest concrete recovery actions. Track for resolution.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose burnout or chronic fatigue syndrome. These require clinical assessment over longer timeframes.
sources: Journal of Occupational Health - Stress Accumulation

title: EDA-Confirmed Stress Response
interpretation: When elevated stress score coincides with high electrodermal activity (EDA), this confirms a genuine sympathetic nervous system activation rather than a scoring artifact. EDA measures sweat gland activity controlled by the sympathetic branch and is harder to fake or misinterpret than algorithmic stress scores.
recommended_agent_action: Use EDA confirmation to increase confidence in stress score accuracy. When both signals agree, the stress reading is more reliable for decision-making.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not assume high EDA always means psychological stress. Physical exertion, temperature, and humidity also affect EDA.
sources: IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering - EDA Sensing

title: Sustained Low Recovery
interpretation: Recovery score below 30 for 5+ consecutive days indicates the body is not adequately recovering between stress exposures. This creates a cumulative deficit that affects immune function, cognitive performance, and emotional resilience. The longer this state persists, the harder recovery becomes.
recommended_agent_action: If recovery score below 30 for 5+ days, escalate to Level 3. Recommend reducing physical and mental load. Suggest dedicated recovery day.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude the user is ill. Low recovery score reflects insufficient recovery opportunity, not necessarily disease.
sources: Stress and Health Journal - Recovery Deficit

title: Burnout Trajectory Warning
interpretation: A 14-day pattern of progressively increasing stress scores, declining recovery scores, and worsening sleep efficiency follows a classic burnout trajectory. The gradual nature makes it invisible to the user day-by-day, but the cumulative trend is significant. Early intervention is far more effective than late-stage burnout management.
recommended_agent_action: Escalate to Level 4 alert. Present the user with a clear visualization of the 14-day trend. Strongly recommend workload adjustment and professional support if available.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose burnout. Burnout is a clinical syndrome diagnosed by healthcare professionals based on multiple criteria.

title: Evening Stress Elevation
interpretation: Stress scores that remain elevated or increase during evening hours when the body should be winding down suggest difficulty disengaging from daytime stressors. This predicts poor sleep quality that night and is a precursor to the stress-sleep feedback loop.
recommended_agent_action: If evening stress scores are consistently higher than afternoon scores for 3+ days, note as pattern. Suggest wind-down routines and screen time reduction.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude the user has an anxiety disorder from evening stress patterns alone.

title: Weekday vs Weekend Stress Differential
interpretation: A large differential between weekday and weekend stress/recovery scores (stress 40%+ higher on weekdays, recovery 30%+ lower) indicates work-related stress dominance. While some differential is normal, extreme differences suggest inadequate coping mechanisms during the work week.
recommended_agent_action: Track weekday vs weekend differential. If extreme, note as insight about work-life balance. Present as observation, not judgment.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude job dissatisfaction or workplace problems from stress patterns alone.
sources: Journal of Occupational Health Psychology - Work Stress Patterns

title: Panic or Acute Anxiety Episode Pattern
interpretation: Sudden spike in stress score above 80, heart rate above 100, and high EDA while sedentary, lasting 10-30 minutes, is consistent with a panic or acute anxiety episode. The key differentiator from cardiac events is the typical duration (self-limiting within 30 minutes) and absence of SpO2 drop.
recommended_agent_action: Monitor duration. If resolves within 30 minutes with HR returning to baseline, log as possible anxiety episode. If SpO2 drops or duration exceeds 30 minutes, escalate to cardiac concern.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not diagnose panic disorder. A single episode does not constitute a disorder. Do not dismiss as 'just anxiety' if accompanied by SpO2 changes.
sources: American Journal of Cardiology - Panic vs Cardiac

title: Post-Illness Recovery Tracking
interpretation: After illness, recovery score and HRV may take 7-14 days to return to pre-illness baselines even after symptoms resolve. Premature return to high activity during this window increases risk of relapse. Monitoring recovery trajectory helps guide safe return to normal activity.
recommended_agent_action: If user was recently ill, track recovery score trajectory. Advise gradual activity increase only as recovery score approaches pre-illness baseline.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude the user is still ill if recovery is slow. Post-viral fatigue is common and does not indicate ongoing infection.

title: Activity Withdrawal Under Stress
interpretation: When stress scores rise and daily step count simultaneously drops significantly (40%+ below baseline), the user may be withdrawing from physical activity due to stress or low energy. While rest is sometimes appropriate, prolonged inactivity during chronic stress can worsen mood and recovery outcomes.
recommended_agent_action: If steps drop 40%+ below baseline concurrent with rising stress for 5+ days, gently suggest light activity. Frame as recovery tool, not obligation.
what_not_to_conclude: Do not conclude depression from reduced activity alone. Many factors affect daily movement patterns.
sources: Lancet Psychiatry - Exercise and Mental Health
